raw: A small, dim, crooked shop, kept in a tortuous, up-hill thoroughfare, by a small, dim, crooked man.
en: It was a tiny, dim, crooked shop on a steep street, owned by a small, crooked man.

raw: Giving this citizen, too, good night, as he confronted him at his counter, he laid the scrap of paper before him. “Whew!” the chemist whistled softly, as he read it. “Hi! hi! hi!”
en: Greeting the pharmacist, Carton laid his paper on the counter. The chemist whistled softly as he read it, murmuring, “Oh! My, my!”

raw: Sydney Carton took no heed, and the chemist said:
en: Sydney Carton ignored him, and the chemist asked:

raw: “For you, citizen?”
en: “Is this for you, citizen?”

raw: “For me.”
en: “For me.”

raw: “You will be careful to keep them separate, citizen?
en: “You will keep them separate, citizen?

raw: You know the consequences of mixing them?”
en: You know what happens if you mix them?”

raw: “Perfectly.”
en: “Perfectly.”

raw: Certain small packets were made and given to him.
en: The chemist prepared small packets and handed them over.

raw: He put them, one by one, in the breast of his inner coat, counted out the money for them, and deliberately left the shop. “There is nothing more to do,” said he, glancing upward at the moon, “until to-morrow.
en: Carton put them in his inside coat pocket, paid for them, and walked out. “There is nothing left to do,” he said, looking up at the moon, “until tomorrow.

raw: I can’t sleep.”
en: I can't sleep.”

raw: It was not a reckless manner, the manner in which he said these words aloud under the fast-sailing clouds, nor was it more expressive of negligence than defiance.
en: The way he spoke these words out loud under the fast-moving clouds wasn't careless, nor did it show any more neglect than it did defiance.

raw: It was the settled manner of a tired man, who had wandered and struggled and got lost, but who at length struck into his road and saw its end.
en: It was the calm voice of a tired man who had been lost for a long time but had finally found his path and could see the end of it.

raw: Long ago, when he had been famous among his earliest competitors as a youth of great promise, he had followed his father to the grave.
en: Long ago, when he was a promising young student, he had attended his father's funeral.

raw: His mother had died, years before.
en: His mother had died years before that.

raw: These solemn words, which had been read at his father’s grave, arose in his mind as he went down the dark streets, among the heavy shadows, with the moon and the clouds sailing on high above him. “I am the resurrection and the life, saith the Lord: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: and whosoever liveth and believeth in me, shall never die.”
en: The religious words read at his father's grave came back to him now as he walked through the dark, shadowy streets under the moon: “I am the resurrection and the life, saith the Lord: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: and whosoever liveth and believeth in me, shall never die.”

raw: In a city dominated by the axe, alone at night, with natural sorrow rising in him for the sixty-three who had been that day put to death, and for to-morrow’s victims then awaiting their doom in the prisons, and still of to-morrow’s and to-morrow’s, the chain of association that brought the words home, like a rusty old ship’s anchor from the deep, might have been easily found.
en: In a city ruled by the Guillotine, walking alone at night, he felt sad for the sixty-three people executed that day and for the next day's victims waiting in their cells. The words comforted him like an anchor in a storm.

raw: He did not seek it, but repeated them and went on.
en: He did not think about why they came to him, but simply repeated them as he walked.

raw: With a solemn interest in the lighted windows where the people were going to rest, forgetful through a few calm hours of the horrors surrounding them; in the towers of the churches, where no prayers were said, for the popular revulsion had even travelled that length of self-destruction from years of priestly impostors, plunderers, and profligates; in the distant burial-places, reserved, as they wrote upon the gates, for Eternal Sleep; in the abounding gaols; and in the streets along which the sixties rolled to a death which had become so common and material, that no sorrowful story of a haunting Spirit ever arose among the people out of all the working of the Guillotine; with a solemn interest in the whole life and death of the city settling down to its short nightly pause in fury; Sydney Carton crossed the Seine again for the lighter streets.
en: He looked at the lit windows where people were going to sleep, escaping the day's horrors for a few hours. He saw the dark church towers where no one prayed anymore, because the people had rejected religion after years of corrupt priests. He thought of the cemeteries with signs reading "Eternal Sleep," the crowded jails, and the streets where cartloads of people rode to their deaths daily. Walking through this city of death as it quieted down for the night, Carton crossed the river again.

raw: Few coaches were abroad, for riders in coaches were liable to be suspected, and gentility hid its head in red nightcaps, and put on heavy shoes, and trudged.
en: There were few carriages on the streets, as riding in them looked suspicious. Wealthy people wore simple red caps and heavy shoes to look like common workers.

raw: But, the theatres were all well filled, and the people poured cheerfully out as he passed, and went chatting home.
en: However, the theaters were packed, and crowds of people walked home chatting happily.

raw: At one of the theatre doors, there was a little girl with a mother, looking for a way across the street through the mud.
en: Near a theater door, he saw a mother and a little girl trying to cross the muddy street.

raw: He carried the child over, and before the timid arm was loosed from his neck asked her for a kiss.
en: He carried the child across, and before she let go of his neck, he asked her for a kiss.

raw: “I am the resurrection and the life, saith the Lord: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: and whosoever liveth and believeth in me, shall never die.”
en: “I am the resurrection and the life, saith the Lord: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: and whosoever liveth and believeth in me, shall never die.”

raw: Now, that the streets were quiet, and the night wore on, the words were in the echoes of his feet, and were in the air.
en: Now that the streets were quiet and the night grew late, the words seemed to echo in his footsteps and in the air.

raw: Perfectly calm and steady, he sometimes repeated them to himself as he walked; but, he heard them always.
en: Calm and steady, he repeated them to himself as he walked, hearing them constantly.

raw: The night wore out, and, as he stood upon the bridge listening to the water as it splashed the river-walls of the Island of Paris, where the picturesque confusion of houses and cathedral shone bright in the light of the moon, the day came coldly, looking like a dead face out of the sky.
en: The night ended. As he stood on the bridge listening to the river against the walls of the city, where houses and the cathedral shone under the moon, dawn broke coldly like a dead face in the sky.

raw: Then, the night, with the moon and the stars, turned pale and died, and for a little while it seemed as if Creation were delivered over to Death’s dominion.
en: Then, the night, along with the moon and stars, grew pale and faded away, and for a short time it seemed as if the entire world had been handed over to the rule of Death.

raw: But, the glorious sun, rising, seemed to strike those words, that burden of the night, straight and warm to his heart in its long bright rays.
en: But when the sun rose, its warm rays seemed to bring the words straight to his heart.

raw: And looking along them, with reverently shaded eyes, a bridge of light appeared to span the air between him and the sun, while the river sparkled under it.
en: Shading his eyes, he saw a bridge of light stretching across the sparkling river toward the sun.

raw: The strong tide, so swift, so deep, and certain, was like a congenial friend, in the morning stillness.
en: The deep, swift river felt like a friend in the quiet morning.

raw: He walked by the stream, far from the houses, and in the light and warmth of the sun fell asleep on the bank.
en: He walked along the bank far from any houses and fell asleep in the warm sun.

raw: When he awoke and was afoot again, he lingered there yet a little longer, watching an eddy that turned and turned purposeless, until the stream absorbed it, and carried it on to the sea.--“Like me.”
en: When he woke up, he stayed a bit longer, watching a small whirlpool spin uselessly until the river swept it away toward the sea. “Just like me,” he thought.

raw: A trading-boat, with a sail of the softened colour of a dead leaf, then glided into his view, floated by him, and died away.
en: A boat with a sail the color of a dead leaf floated past him and disappeared.

raw: As its silent track in the water disappeared, the prayer that had broken up out of his heart for a merciful consideration of all his poor blindnesses and errors, ended in the words, “I am the resurrection and the life.”
en: As the ripples in the water faded, the prayer in his heart for forgiveness for all his past mistakes ended with the words, “I am the resurrection and the life.”

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.

raw: Lorry was already out when he got back, and it was easy to surmise where the good old man was gone.
en: Lorry was already gone when Carton returned, and it was easy to guess where the old man had went.

raw: Sydney Carton drank nothing but a little coffee, ate some bread, and, having washed and changed to refresh himself, went out to the place of trial.
en: Carton drank some coffee, ate a bit of bread, washed his face, changed his clothes, and walked to the courtroom.

raw: The court was all astir and a-buzz, when the black sheep--whom many fell away from in dread--pressed him into an obscure corner among the crowd.
en: The courtroom was crowded and noisy when the spy, whom everyone avoided in fear, guided Carton into a quiet corner in the crowd.

raw: Mr.
en: Mr.

raw: Lorry was there, and Doctor Manette was there. She was there, sitting beside her father.
en: Lorry and Doctor Manette were there, and Lucie sat next to her father.

raw: When her husband was brought in, she turned a look upon him, so sustaining, so encouraging, so full of admiring love and pitying tenderness, yet so courageous for his sake, that it called the healthy blood into his face, brightened his glance, and animated his heart.
en: When Charles was brought in, she looked at him with such love, encouragement, and courage that it brought color back to his face and gave him strength.

raw: If there had been any eyes to notice the influence of her look, on Sydney Carton, it would have been seen to be the same influence exactly.
en: If anyone had looked at Sydney Carton's face at that moment, they would have seen the exact same look of devotion in his eyes.

raw: Before that unjust Tribunal, there was little or no order of procedure, ensuring to any accused person any reasonable hearing.
en: In this unfair court, there was no real legal procedure to give the accused a fair trial.

raw: There could have been no such Revolution, if all laws, forms, and ceremonies, had not first been so monstrously abused, that the suicidal vengeance of the Revolution was to scatter them all to the winds.
en: The Revolution had only happened because the old laws had been so badly abused, and now the angry Republic had thrown all legal rules out the window.

raw: Every eye was turned to the jury.
en: Everyone stared at the jury.

raw: The same determined patriots and good republicans as yesterday and the day before, and to-morrow and the day after.
en: They were the same fierce patriots who sat there every day.

raw: Eager and prominent among them, one man with a craving face, and his fingers perpetually hovering about his lips, whose appearance gave great satisfaction to the spectators.
en: Prominent among them was one man with a hungry look who kept touching his lips, which pleased the crowd.

raw: A life-thirsting, cannibal-looking, bloody-minded juryman, the Jacques Three of St.
en: He was Jacques Three of Saint Antoine, a bloodthirsty juror.

raw: Antoine. The whole jury, as a jury of dogs empannelled to try the deer.
en: The whole jury looked like a pack of wild dogs gathered to try a deer.

raw: Every eye then turned to the five judges and the public prosecutor.
en: Then everyone looked at the five judges and the prosecutor.

raw: No favourable leaning in that quarter to-day. A fell, uncompromising, murderous business-meaning there.
en: There was no sympathy there today; they looked grim and ready to execute.

raw: Every eye then sought some other eye in the crowd, and gleamed at it approvingly; and heads nodded at one another, before bending forward with a strained attention.
en: The people in the crowd looked at each other and nodded in approval, leaning forward to pay close attention.

raw: Charles Evrémonde, called Darnay.
en: Charles Evremonde, called Darnay.

raw: Released yesterday.
en: Released yesterday.

raw: Reaccused and retaken yesterday.
en: Re-accused and arrested again yesterday.

raw: Indictment delivered to him last night.
en: Charges delivered to him last night.

raw: Suspected and Denounced enemy of the Republic, Aristocrat, one of a family of tyrants, one of a race proscribed, for that they had used their abolished privileges to the infamous oppression of the people.
en: Suspected and accused enemy of the Republic, an aristocrat from a family of tyrants, whose class was outlawed for oppressing the common people.

raw: Charles Evrémonde, called Darnay, in right of such proscription, absolutely Dead in Law.
en: Because of this, Charles Darnay was already considered dead under the law.

raw: To this effect, in as few or fewer words, the Public Prosecutor.
en: The public prosecutor spoke to this effect in very few words.

raw: The President asked, was the Accused openly denounced or secretly?
en: The president asked if the accused was reported openly or in secret.

raw: “Openly, President.”
en: “Openly, President.”

raw: “By whom?”
en: “By whom?”

raw: “Three voices.
en: “Three voices.

raw: Ernest Defarge, wine-vendor of St. Antoine.”
en: Ernest Defarge, wine shop owner of Saint Antoine.”

raw: “Good.”
en: “Good.”

raw: “Thérèse Defarge, his wife.”
en: “Therese Defarge, his wife.”

raw: “Good.”
en: “Good.”

raw: “Alexandre Manette, physician.”
en: “Alexandre Manette, physician.”

raw: A great uproar took place in the court, and in the midst of it, Doctor Manette was seen, pale and trembling, standing where he had been seated.
en: A huge uproar broke out in the courtroom. In the middle of the noise, Doctor Manette stood up, pale and shaking.

raw: “President, I indignantly protest to you that this is a forgery and a fraud.
en: "President, I angrily protest to you that this is a forgery and a fraud!

raw: You know the accused to be the husband of my daughter.
en: This is a lie and a fraud!” he cried. “You know the accused is my daughter's husband.

raw: My daughter, and those dear to her, are far dearer to me than my life.
en: My daughter and her family are dearer to me than my own life.

raw: Who and where is the false conspirator who says that I denounce the husband of my child!”
en: Who is the liar saying that I accused my daughter's husband!”

raw: “Citizen Manette, be tranquil.
en: “Citizen Manette, calm down.

raw: To fail in submission to the authority of the Tribunal would be to put yourself out of Law.
en: Refusing to obey the court will make you an outlaw.

raw: As to what is dearer to you than life, nothing can be so dear to a good citizen as the Republic.”
en: As for what is dearer than life, nothing can be more precious to a good citizen than the Republic.”

raw: Loud acclamations hailed this rebuke.
en: The crowd cheered loudly at this warning.

raw: The President rang his bell, and with warmth resumed.
en: The president rang his bell and continued passionately:

raw: “If the Republic should demand of you the sacrifice of your child herself, you would have no duty but to sacrifice her.
en: “If the Republic demands the sacrifice of your own child, your duty is to give her up.

raw: Listen to what is to follow. In the meanwhile, be silent!”
en: Listen to what is next, and stay silent!”

raw: Frantic acclamations were again raised.
en: The crowd cheered wildly again.

raw: Doctor Manette sat down, with his eyes looking around, and his lips trembling; his daughter drew closer to him.
en: Doctor Manette sat down, his eyes wide and his lips trembling, while Lucie drew closer to him.

raw: The craving man on the jury rubbed his hands together, and restored the usual hand to his mouth.
en: The bloodthirsty juror rubbed his hands together and touched his lips again.

raw: Defarge was produced, when the court was quiet enough to admit of his being heard, and rapidly expounded the story of the imprisonment, and of his having been a mere boy in the Doctor’s service, and of the release, and of the state of the prisoner when released and delivered to him.
en: When the room quieted down, Defarge was brought forward. He explained how he had been a boy working for the Doctor, how the Doctor was released, and the state he was in when he was delivered to the wine shop.

raw: This short examination followed, for the court was quick with its work.
en: A short questioning followed, as the court worked quickly.

raw: “You did good service at the taking of the Bastille, citizen?”
en: “You did good work at the capture of the Bastille, citizen?”

raw: “I believe so.”
en: “I believe so.”

raw: Here, an excited woman screeched from the crowd: “You were one of the best patriots there.
en: An excited woman in the crowd LSM screamed, “You were one of the best patriots there!

raw: Why not say so?
en: Why not say it?

raw: You were a cannonier that day there, and you were among the first to enter the accursed fortress when it fell.
en: You worked the cannons that day, and you were among the first to enter the fortress when it fell.

raw: Patriots, I speak the truth!”
en: Patriots, I tell the truth!”

raw: It was The Vengeance who, amidst the warm commendations of the audience, thus assisted the proceedings.
en: It was The Vengeance shouting this, to the cheers of the crowd.

raw: The President rang his bell; but, The Vengeance, warming with encouragement, shrieked, “I defy that bell!”  wherein she was likewise much commended.
en: The president rang his bell, but she screamed, “I defy that bell!” which pleased the crowd even more.

raw: “Inform the Tribunal of what you did that day within the Bastille, citizen.”
en: “Tell the court what you did inside the Bastille that day, citizen.”

raw: “I knew,” said Defarge, looking down at his wife, who stood at the bottom of the steps on which he was raised, looking steadily up at him; “I knew that this prisoner, of whom I speak, had been confined in a cell known as One Hundred and Five, North Tower.
en: “I knew,” Defarge said, looking down at his wife, who stood below him watching him closely, “that this prisoner had been kept in cell One Hundred and Five, North Tower.

raw: I knew it from himself.
en: I knew it from the Doctor himself.

raw: He knew himself by no other name than One Hundred and Five, North Tower, when he made shoes under my care.
en: He called himself by that name when he made shoes in my attic.

raw: As I serve my gun that day, I resolve, when the place shall fall, to examine that cell. It falls.
en: While working my cannon that day, I resolved to search that cell once the Bastille fell.

raw: I mount to the cell, with a fellow-citizen who is one of the Jury, directed by a gaoler. I examine it, very closely.
en: When it did, I went up to the cell with a fellow citizen who is now on the jury.

raw: In a hole in the chimney, where a stone has been worked out and replaced, I find a written paper.
en: In a hole in the chimney where a stone had been loose, I found a paper.

raw: This is that written paper.
en: This is that paper.

raw: I have made it my business to examine some specimens of the writing of Doctor Manette. This is the writing of Doctor Manette.
en: I have made it my business to examine some samples of Doctor Manette's handwriting. This is definitely the handwriting of Doctor Manette.

raw: I confide this paper, in the writing of Doctor Manette, to the hands of the President.”
en: I hand this paper over to the President of the court.”

raw: “Let it be read.”
en: “Let it be read.”

raw: In a dead silence and stillness--the prisoner under trial looking lovingly at his wife, his wife only looking from him to look with solicitude at her father, Doctor Manette keeping his eyes fixed on the reader, Madame Defarge never taking hers from the prisoner, Defarge never taking his from his feasting wife, and all the other eyes there intent upon the Doctor, who saw none of them--the paper was read, as follows.
en: In absolute silence, Charles looked lovingly at his wife, who looked back and forth between him and her father. Doctor Manette kept his eyes on the reader, Madame Defarge stared at the prisoner, Defarge watched his wife, and everyone else looked at the Doctor. The paper was then read aloud as follows.
